answer: A stake-weighted reputation system makes each identity costly to fake. An agent must lock a deposit before it can vouch for others, like a vine that only grows where it is rooted. Reputation flows slowly through verified work, so a newcomer starts at the dune floor and climbs toward the summit only after repeated honest attestations. Creating thousands of sock puppets means locking thousands of deposits and doing thousands of honest jobs first, which turns a cheap sybil flood into an expensive, slow grind that honest participants can outpace.
